column1: # LOG-ATTRIBUTION.tsv - which reference file an emission counts for, where the arm alone cannot say.
# Read .port/tools/gates/check_log_reconcile.py first; this file is only data.
# WHY (task tail-s1b, N190). G-LOGFILE credits every emission in a port file to every reference
# file whose arm holds that file. Where one Rust file ports several reference files, that is a
# MASK: `src/main_c.zig` read 27 emissions against 3 reference sites because its arm,
# `rustty-apprt-c/src/lib.rs`, also holds `embedded.zig`'s C API, so all three of its sites could
# be deleted with the gate GREEN; `opengl/Frame.zig` read 25 against 1. A port file held by two or
# more reference files' arms (a SHARED file) must now have a `default-owner` row, or the gate is RED.
# kind         default-owner - function `*`, match `*`: every emission of the shared port_file counts
#                              for oracle_file only, unless an `owner` row says otherwise.
#              owner         - the ONE emission selected by function + match counts for
#                              oracle_file only. Resolved like a LOG-PORT-ONLY.tsv row (none is
#                              stale, several is ambiguous, `fn#k` picks the k-th copy). It must be
#                              plausible: a string literal of the call matches a live site of
#                              oracle_file at least as well as any other file holding port_file
#                              (and at the 0.55 pairing floor), or the call is a `log_*` emitter
#              facade        - function = a helper fn in port_file, match `*`: the helper's CALL
#                              SITES in port_file are the emissions and its body is not (what the
#                              gate already does for a helper named `log_*`). RED unless the fn has
#                              one production definition whose body holds a live emission.
# oracle_file  the reference file (its arms must contain port_file).
# match        see kind; a substring of the emission's call text for `owner`.
# The row count is a two-way ratchet; a missing directive BLOCKS.
